module_memory_caches.stacking: React Query refetch after 5m re-invokes the fetcher, which serves the SAME bytes from the module cache until 60m elapses -- effective client TTL for distribution + aum-metrics is up to 60min without a page reload

browser_http_cache.state: NO Cache-Control on mdpf responses; ETag + Last-Modified present
browser_http_cache.consequence: RFC 9111 heuristic freshness applies (typically 10% of (now - Last-Modified)). A day-old artifact earns ~2.4h of silent browser-cache freshness; grows with artifact age. UNGOVERNED layer.
browser_http_cache.invalidation_mechanism: none (no header to govern it); conditional revalidation via ETag only after heuristic expiry

t3b_clash_flags: F1 NO-CLIENT-TTL: mdpf responses carry no Cache-Control (injector /json/-scoped since router v6 flip; S3 metadata unset by publisher). Browser heuristic caching is the operative client policy and it GROWS with artifact age (~2.4h at one day old) -- a daily publish window can be invisible to returning browsers for hours, and no invalidation reaches a browser cache. T3.B options: extend injector stamping to /platinum/mdpf/ OR stamp CacheControl at the publisher put_object. FLAG ONLY, not fixed.

F2 NO-PUBLISH-INVALIDATION: publisher fires no CF invalidation; edge staleness after a publish is bounded by DefaultTTL 300s. Acceptable for a daily clock, but T2.C's publish-window ruling should state it explicitly; if T2.C lands a tighter-than-5min freshness expectation the 300s tail clashes.

F3 60-MIN-MODULE-CACHE: accountDistributionByFirmCache + aumMetricsByFirmCache (60m, in-memory, no invalidation path short of reload) sit ABOVE every HTTP layer -- an open tab spans the publish window showing pre-publish numbers for up to 60m regardless of any edge-side T3.B design. Changing this requires a portal release, not an infra change.

F4 ROLLBACK-SEMANTICS: DataRefresh rollback invalidates /api/general/* (purges mdpf edge cache) while NOT restoring platinum/mdpf objects -- a rollback around the mdpf window re-pulls the SAME post-publish mdpf bytes with a fresh TTL. Coherent today; worth stating in T3.B so nobody reads the invalidation as a rollback of mdpf.
findings_non_blocking: N1 DECLARATIVE-DRIFT: aum.ts:520-523,560 + portal-proxy.ts:497-501,515-519 comments still claim '/api/general/* -> /json/*' rewrite and json/mdpf/* serve keys; deployed router v6 rewrites mdpf to /platinum/mdpf/. N2 DEAD-ROOT-ROUTE: portal-proxy.ts getMdpfAggregateAUATimeSeries() targets /api/general/mdpf/aggregate-aua-timeseries.json -> platinum/mdpf/aggregate-aua-timeseries.json which DOES NOT EXIST (measured 403). Zero page consumers (ModelPortfolios uses ByFirm('global')). Dead code candidate.

N3 AUM-METRICS-SPARSE-BY-DESIGN: platinum/mdpf/{scope}/aum-metrics.json exists only for cottonwood; the only enabled fetch is cottonwood (ModelPortfolios.tsx:488 enabled predicate). Not a defect; recorded so nobody reads the absent keys as gaps.

N4 QUERY-STRING-NOT-IN-CACHE-KEY: ce00305d has qs=none -- ?refresh= style cache-busting does NOT create a distinct edge entry on mdpf routes (unlike advisor-by-firm which whitelists). Any T3.B buster design must use the path, not a query string.
